div.span: row filters and column masks, or an ABAC policy at catalog scope

The platform enforces. Resolves per caller, and holds across the agent and Teams hops.
Test it against a case it has to deny.

div.span: the service principal is the identity
Every human calling through it sees the union of what the SP may read, with no differentiation between them. On this path that is the whole of your access control.

div.span:
Resolve groups per request from the caller's own token. A naming convention works until access is a combination of columns; then use a declared table.
Refuse on error. Empty is the default. Malformed raises.
Test the denial path: the happy path passes either way.

div.span: move enforcement back into the database

Your ACL becomes a row-level security policy again, evaluated by the engine rather than by your retrieval code.
A governance argument rather than a latency one, and the stronger of the two.

div.span:
1. Point the filter at something that must return nothing, and watch it return nothing. A control you have only seen succeed is a control you have not tested.
2. Make your two zeros distinguishable: "no entitlement" and "something broke" look identical from outside.
3. Assert on the identity that produced the answer. An answer arriving tells you nothing about who it was filtered for.
